Chapter 10: The Lucky Girl at the Desk in Front

At nine o'clock, the exam officially began.

After the test papers were handed out, the girl hunched over her desk and began to fill in her information.

The sunlight dyed the edges of her ponytail a golden yellow. The ends of her hair were slightly split. The fine hairs on the side of her left cheek made her seem all the more serene.

Jiang Nian withdrew his gaze from her fair neck, his mood lightening.

It would be a lie to say he wasn't nervous. Although he had relied on Memory Time to imprint all the memorizable subject knowledge in his brain, this was, after all, the exam that would decide his third-year placement.

But having a pretty girl at the desk in front of him might be a good omen.

The two days of exams passed in a flash.

The girl at the front desk had indeed brought him good luck, from the Chinese language exam all the way to the final English exam. He performed as usual, perhaps even better than usual.

After some time, Jiang Nian also learned the girl's name: Zhang Ningzhi.

During the math exam, he had borrowed her eraser.

Before the English exam, Jiang Nian thought about how he had leeched off her luck. He probably wouldn't see her again after the exams were over, so he mulled it over and decided to do something.

So, while expressing his thanks, he gave Zhang Ningzhi a carton of milk with fruit bits.

If they were outside school, no one would dare accept this. After all, what girl would dare drink something handed to her by a strange guy? But in school, the risk wasn't as great.

Zhang Ningzhi hesitated for a moment, then said thank you and accepted it.

He didn't think much of it. During the final English exam, the classroom was so quiet that only the sound of scratching pens could be heard.

Smelling the scent of ink from the test paper, Jiang Nian's hands trembled slightly. Perhaps it was because this was the final exam, or perhaps it was because of his half-drenched short-sleeved shirt.

A gust of wind blew in from outside the door, causing his row of pearly white teeth to chatter, a sour, numbing sensation.

His heart beat like a drum, and his head was burning up.

"It's fine," he muttered to himself while working on the paper, "Chinese should be at least a hundred, Math should be a hundred, and Science comprehensive over two hundred and ten."

"If I get twenty for the English essay and lose ten points on listening, a hundred and thirty for English is a sure thing."

Five hundred forty was just his estimated base score. For a test with a total of seven hundred fifty points, it wasn't a particularly high score, but it was already very high for a parallel class.

If these exams were the real Gaokao, it would be more than enough to get into a decent Tier 1 university.

Jiang Nian estimated that after this placement test was over, he should be able to get first place in the class. If things went smoothly, moving up to the Science Olympiad class shouldn't be a problem.

At four-thirty in the afternoon, everyone left the examination hall, packing their things to return to the classroom and tidy up their desks.

The exams had taken up the whole weekend. The Sunday evening self-study session was canceled for a break. This meant that from the end of the exam, the entire evening was free.

The classroom was in an uproar. Some chose to head straight to the internet cafe; others chose to put their desks back in order before leaving.

The classroom, the hallways, the entire third-year building was exceptionally noisy and lively. Some were discussing the test papers. Some were gathered around teachers chatting, occasionally clapping their hands or regretfully stamping their feet and beating their chests.

There were quite a few people visiting other classes, and many new faces appeared in their classroom. They were either gathered in groups of several, checking their calculations on scratch paper, talking and laughing loudly, or making plans to go to the internet cafe.

Jiang Nian bent down and easily lifted his heavy book basket. Just as he straightened up, he saw Zhou Yuting walk in. Her eyes scanned the classroom, likely looking for someone to help move her books.

As he passed by her, Zhou Yuting called out to him.

"Jiang Nian, can you help me move my books? They're really heavy, I can't carry them."

—

"When a member of the opposite sex who you've practically fallen out with, but not officially, asks for your help, it's best to pretend you didn't hear."

Jiang Nian paid her no mind, walking two steps forward before turning back.

"Ah? Were you calling me?"

"Yeah, can you help me move my books?" Zhou Yuting said. Perhaps because of the weekend exams, she was wearing a white cotton dress. "And help Yingying move hers too, while you're at it." Sun Yingying was Zhou Yuting's superficial best friend, and she had a thing for Liu Feipeng.

"Oh, why don't you ask Le Zhi to help you?" Jiang Nian glanced at her, a slight curve on his lips. "He'd definitely be happy to move your books for you."

Zhou Yuting froze at his words. Of course she knew Le Zhi would help her. But Le Zhi was too annoying. Jiang Nian wouldn't ramble on and on, and he was also good-looking.

Although Zhou Yuting would never consider a poor guy like Jiang Nian for a boyfriend, having one more handsome simp would raise her value.

"He's too annoying. It's better to ask you."

Jiang Nian had originally wanted to bring up her birthday party to mock her, but on second thought, he was about to move to a better class, so why waste his breath?

Even if he made a girl cry, he wouldn't win anything.

"Mm."

He responded coldly, turned with his book basket in his arms, and walked away.

Zhou Yuting stood there, originally thinking Jiang Nian would come back to help her after putting his books down. But after waiting a long time and seeing no sign of him, she went out to look, almost fuming with rage.

Jiang Nian had gone to the class next door to help another girl move her books.

She swore that she would never look Jiang Nian in the eye again. She would never say another word to him, either. Did he think that would make her feel insecure!

"It's okay, I can move them myself." Xu Qianqian said, looking at the surrounding stares, a little embarrassed. "They'll ask you to help them move theirs in a bit."

"So what if they do? It's no trouble," Jiang Nian said with a look of indifference.

"No, that won't do. Their books are too heavy," Xu Qianqian frowned. "Just leave after this. Wait for me at the school gate, I'll be there in a bit."

Without realizing it, Xu Qianqian had already gotten used to going home with Jiang Nian.

"Alright then."

After moving the books, Jiang Nian left the academic building, glancing back at his classroom one last time. He suddenly felt a little flicker of anticipation, looking forward to the day the results came out.

Today was Sunday, so they should all be out by tomorrow. The class changes would happen next week.

A short while later, Xu Qianqian came out with her schoolbag on her back. She looked around and spotted Jiang Nian. She tightened her bag straps and walked towards him.

A few nearby students saw this scene and couldn't help but stop and watch.

They originally thought they were about to witness some puppy love gossip, but the two just walked off calmly, even taking out their test papers.

"Do you think you can get five hundred forty this time?" she asked with a frown. "I heard that under normal circumstances, you need at least five fifty to be safe when transferring up from a lower-tier class."

The two walked side by side. Jiang Nian's heart nearly stopped when he heard that.

Wait, buddy, I have a cheat, you can't be serious, right? Are you people in the Olympiad class all freaking Ultraman Seven? Aren't there any who got in through connections?

When Xu Qianqian learned of Jiang Nian's naive thoughts, she couldn't help but let out a "che."

"It's precisely because there are people with connections that you need a higher score. They can stay in the Olympiad class even with four hundred points. What does transferring classes have to do with them?"

Too realistic. This was how a society based on personal connections in a small county worked.

"Alright, let me check the English answers with you," Jiang Nian took a deep breath. "How did you do on English this time? A perfect score again?"

Xu Qianqian snorted, her expression a mix of three parts mockery, three parts pride, three parts nonchalance, and one part proud little swan.

"What do you think?"

Neat rows of electrical wires sliced through the dusk as night quietly fell.

(End of Chapter)
